chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Zakariyya who said:

I was a Christian, so I became a Muslim. So I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'My family are upon the religion of Christianity, so I am with them in one house and I eat from their vessels.' He (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Do they eat the flesh of the swine?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'There is no problem.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a Muslim to eat from the dishes of non-Muslims who do not eat pork?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'original purity' (al-asl fi al-anzar al-salah) for the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab), distinguishing their general purity from the specific impurity of pork. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that since Christians do not consume pork, their vessels remain ritually pure for use, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the impurity of Ahl al-Kitab is limited to their meat rather than their entire household items. This ruling facilitates social cohesion and practical daily life for converts maintaining ties with non-Muslim family members.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam,f rom Muawiya Bin Wahab, from Zakariyya Bin Ibrahim who said,

‘I was a Christian, so I became a Muslim. So I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘My family are upon the religion of Christianity, so I happen to be with them in one house, and I eat from their vessels’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Are they eating the flesh of the swine?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab from Zakariya ibn Ibrahim who has said the following:

“I was a Christian, then became a Muslim and said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘People of my family are Christians. I live with them in one house and eat in their utensils. He (the Imam) asked, ‘Do they eat pork?’ I replied, ‘No, they do not eat pork.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.
